target.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin registration transaction snapshot used a **shallow clone** (`{ ...value }` for object fields). This left nested registration objects (e.g. hook/tool/config entries) **shared by reference** with the live registry. When a transaction mutated a nested property in place and then rolled back, the snapshot's shallow copy did not capture the nested change, so the mutated state survived rollback and orphan registers stayed in the manifest cache. (#107514)

## Why This Change Was Made

`snapshotPluginRegistry` must produce a true point-in-time copy so `restorePluginRegistry` can fully revert every in-transaction change, including nested config mutations — not just top-level array pushes or field replacements. `structuredClone` is already the project-standard deep copy (used in `hooks.ts`, `installed-plugin-index-*`, etc.) and `PluginRegistry` is pure data (arrays + Maps + strings), so it clones cleanly.

## User Impact

Plugin registration install/enable timeouts that roll back no longer leave orphaned registers / stale nested config behind in the manifest cache. No behavior change for successful commits.

## Evidence

- Root cause confirmed in `src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.ts` `snapshotPluginRegistry` (shallow `{...value}`).
- Added regression test `rolls back nested config mutations on a registered entry (#107514)` — fails against the old shallow clone, passes with `structuredClone`.
- `pnpm lint` + `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.
- Freshness gate: `git diff origin/main` confirms the shallow clone is still present on latest `main`; no competing open PR references #107514.
